notes: All evals assume the subagent runs with cwd set to a real repo checkout with a GitHub remote (gh available). Issue creation is the deliverable; when a live gh is unavailable, assert on the issue-body drafts the agent proposes before create. Each case exercises one of the three sources — plan file (default), PRD issue, raw conversation — and pins the source-reference header the issue body must use.

evals.name: plan-file-source-default
evals.prompt: break this plan into grabbable GitHub issues
evals.expected_output: The agent uses the ./plans/*.md file as the source, drafts tracer-bullet vertical slices, quizzes the user (HITL/AFK, blockers, granularity), and creates issues in dependency order whose bodies open with a '## Source plan' header referencing the plan path.

files.content:
# Auth MVP — Implementation Plan

Source PRD: #12

## Phase 1 — Session foundation

Data model: `users(id, email, password_hash)`, `sessions(id, user_id, expires_at)`.
Module boundary: `auth` package owns hashing and session issuance behind a `SessionStore` interface.

User story 1: As a user I can sign up with email + password.
User story 2: As a user I can log in and receive a session cookie.
Acceptance: signup persists a hashed password; login returns a valid session cookie.

## Phase 2 — Protected routes

User story 3: As a user I stay logged in across requests.
Acceptance: a request with a valid session cookie reaches a protected route; an expired one is rejected.

assertions.text: The agent identifies ./plans/auth-mvp.md as the source (plan file is the default source) without asking for a PRD number or conversation
The agent proposes tracer-bullet vertical slices, each a complete end-to-end path rather than a single-layer horizontal slice
The agent presents the breakdown as a numbered list marking each slice HITL or AFK with blocked-by relationships, and quizzes the user on granularity and dependencies before creating anything
Each created (or drafted) issue body opens with a '## Source plan' header referencing `./plans/auth-mvp.md`
No issue body uses '## Parent PRD' or '## Source conversation' as its source-reference header
Issues are created in dependency order so blocked-by fields reference real earlier issue numbers
The source plan file ./plans/auth-mvp.md is not modified

evals.name: prd-issue-source
evals.prompt: cut implementation tickets from PRD issue #12
evals.expected_output: With no ./plans/*.md present, the agent fetches PRD issue #12 with gh, drafts tracer-bullet slices, quizzes the user, and creates issues whose bodies open with a '## Parent PRD' header referencing #12.

assertions.text: The agent uses the PRD GitHub issue #12 as the source (fetches it with gh issue view rather than looking only for a plan file)
The agent proposes tracer-bullet vertical slices and quizzes the user on HITL/AFK, blockers, and granularity before creating issues
Each created (or drafted) issue body opens with a '## Parent PRD' header referencing #12
No issue body uses '## Source plan' or '## Source conversation' as its source-reference header
Issues are created in dependency order with blocked-by fields referencing real earlier issue numbers
The parent PRD issue #12 is not closed or modified

evals.name: conversation-source
evals.prompt: we just spent an hour hashing this out in chat — turn our conversation into GitHub issues. We agreed to add a CSV export: a button on the reports page hits a new /export endpoint that streams the current report as CSV, gated behind the existing auth middleware. Then a follow-up to let users pick which columns are included.
evals.expected_output: With no plan file and no PRD issue, the agent treats the in-context conversation as the source, drafts tracer-bullet slices, quizzes the user, and creates issues whose bodies open with a '## Source conversation' header.

assertions.text: The agent treats the in-context conversation as the source (does not demand a ./plans/*.md file or a PRD issue number)
The agent proposes tracer-bullet vertical slices grounded in the conversation (e.g. an /export endpoint slice, then a column-selection slice) and quizzes the user before creating issues
Each created (or drafted) issue body opens with a '## Source conversation' header
No issue body uses '## Source plan' or '## Parent PRD' as its source-reference header
Issues are created in dependency order with blocked-by fields referencing real earlier issue numbers
